title: JARVIS: Personal AI Assistant
description:
JARVIS is an always-on personal AI assistant I built and run on my own private server, reachable 24/7 from web, WhatsApp, Discord, and voice. It orchestrates LLM-powered agents that manage my calendar, email, smart-home routines, web scraping pipelines, cron automations, and even deploy code — with persistent memory across sessions and a full audit trail of every action.

The stack includes a FastAPI/uvicorn gateway with a live web dashboard (sessions, cron jobs, model usage, skills, and plugin management), multi-provider LLM routing with automatic failover, a browser-automation engine, and speech-to-text plus neural TTS for voice calls. Everything is self-hosted and observable from the Control Center shown in the screenshots. Live demo: jarvis.enriquecodes.com.

impact.impact_1: Runs 20+ scheduled automations (data pipelines, alerts, reports) unattended, 24/7, on a single self-hosted box
impact.impact_2: Multi-provider LLM routing with dual-key rotation keeps the assistant online through provider outages
impact.impact_3: One Control Center dashboard to manage sessions, cron jobs, models, and skills across every channel

title: Reconciler Pro
description:
Reconciler Pro is an AI-powered SaaS platform I designed and built that reconciles point-of-sale (POS) data for event-ticket brokers: it connects to a broker's POS and bank feeds, matches purchases against settlements, and flags discrepancies automatically.

At its core is a matching engine I designed: a rules-based system combined with machine-learning models and custom matching algorithms that automatically match purchases with inventory and settlements — scoring candidate matches, tolerating real-world noise (name variations, timing gaps, fees), and escalating only genuine exceptions for human review.

The frontend is a React + Vite + TypeScript app (shadcn/ui, Tailwind) with a dashboard for reconciliation runs, the matching rules engine, POS provider integrations, bank syncing, transaction drill-downs, and subscription billing. The backend runs on Supabase (Postgres, auth, row-level security) with edge functions for provider sync jobs.

I took it from concept to a working product with two pilot brokers: multi-tenant auth, POS credential onboarding with MFA handling, and automated daily reconciliation pipelines.

impact.impact_1: Designed custom matching algorithms + ML models that auto-match POS purchases to inventory and bank settlements, flagging only true exceptions
impact.impact_2: Full multi-tenant SaaS: auth, organization scoping, and row-level security on Supabase
impact.impact_3: Integrations architecture for POS providers and bank feeds (ClearConnection) with MFA-aware onboarding

title: Broker Copilot
description:
As part of my work with Ticketflipping, I am building Broker Copilot, a ChatGPT-style assistant that lets ticket brokers chat with their own point-of-sale data. It connects to a customer's Skybox or Lysted POS account and answers questions about their inventory, sales, and pricing in plain language.

The agentic workflow is built with Langflow on top of Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, self-deployed on a private EC2 instance. My work spans the full product: designing the Langflow flow and tiered agent prompts (lite, pro, elite), building the Django chat application, integrating the POS data, and deploying it via AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Broker Copilot is set to launch publicly in 2026.

impact.impact_1: Gives brokers natural-language access to their entire POS history, with no exports or manual queries needed
impact.impact_2: Tiered prompt design (lite, pro, elite) serves every subscription level from a single Langflow deployment

title: Social Control Hub
description:
Social Control Hub is an AI-powered content platform I built end to end: it not only tracks and analyzes social media performance across YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok in a single dashboard (reach, engagement, and growth over a rolling 30-day window), it also creates the videos themselves with AI.

The core is an AI video-creation pipeline I designed and built: it goes from idea to finished video using AI for scripting, voiceover, and visuals, orchestrated through multiple automated stages — each with built-in safeguards, guardrails, and watchdogs so a failure at any stage is caught and recovered automatically. The pipeline was built from day one to run as a product for automatic video content creation: faceless channels get produced, quality-checked, and published with minimal human intervention.

I own the entire system: the AI generation pipeline, the data ingestion from each platform, the data model, and the dashboard — consolidating views, followers, likes, and comments from every channel into unified totals, with per-profile and per-platform breakdowns, daily time-series charts, and one-click TSV and Markdown exports.

impact.impact_1: AI video pipeline that produces finished videos automatically (AI scripting, voiceover, and visuals) with stage-by-stage safeguards, guardrails, and automatic failure recovery
impact.impact_2: Built as a product for automatic AI video content creation, powering faceless channels end to end
impact.impact_3: Analytics dashboard tracking 2.4M views and 16.5K followers across 9 channels on YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok with daily refresh

title: RAG AI Assistant
description:
As part of my work with Ticketflipping, I developed an AI Assistant that uses Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to reply to user's messages using 7 years of Slack messages, 100+ training videos and demo calls, and other internal resources. These total to 250K+ vector objects.

My work was from beginning to end, which includes data treatment, embedding, Langflow process design, designing the agent prompts, creating and managing the Redis instance, deploying Langflow to private EC2 instance, creating and setting up the Slack Bot, and testing the tool.

impact.impact_1: Unlocked access to 7+ years of institutional knowledge for all team members
impact.impact_2: Handles 500+ user queries monthly, reducing support burden on senior team members

title: Ticketmaster Heat Map
description:

title: Implementation of Server Side Caching (Redis)
description:
High loading times were a major issue among Ticketflipping's customers, aand the issue continued to increase thanks to the hike in entertainment events during the last few years. Initially the site was created to use client-side caching for tables with 20K+ rows, but once the event count passed 40K, many customers would wait from 10 to 40 seconds for one of the pages to load.

I was tasked with implementing any solution to the issue. After some research, I found Redis and implemented it in the backend of Ticketflipping's Django app. My work was from beginning to end, which includes setting up the Redis instance, creating the cache logic, coding the backend operations, and designing and constructing the cached tables and advanced filtering. Since then, I have brought 34 of Ticketflipping's views to use Redis caching.

impact.impact_1: Reduced loading time for all pages by 95%

title: Flare: Event Data Platform
description:
Although this does not constitute to a specific project, I have dedicated over 20% of my time with Ticketflipping to work on their entertainment event data platform, Flare. The platform is the heart of Ticketflipping's business, and is used by all their customers to manage events, view their data, set up alerts for ticket count and price, and conducting research. Flare counts with many features, some of which are viewing event historical data, tracking event sales, or managing a portfolio of events. Flare tracks around 100K events in the US, and partial covery of the rest of the world. This includes primary markets (Ticketmaster, AXS, tickets.com) and secondary markets (StubHub, Tickpick, Seatgeek, Viviseats, etc.).

My work in this platform consists on Debugging Issues, developing features, explanding coverage to other markets (Tickets.com and Tickpick), and keeping up with user's requests.

impact.impact_1: Ticketflipping's community received 1-2 major updates per month
impact.impact_2: 15-30 bugs/month are fixed and deployed within an average of 3 days

My work involved creating robust scraping mechanisms that can handle different website layouts, implementing rate limiting and proxy rotation, developing error handling and retry mechanisms, and ensuring data quality and consistency across different sources.

title: New Database Schema for Flare
description:
As part of my work with Ticketflipping, I was tasked with developing a new database schema for Flare. Ticketflipping was initilly created to serve an specific market, which is why a new schema was needed in order to scale the opertion. The new schema was designed to improve the performance and scalability of the platform, and to make it easier to maintain and extend.

My work involved designing the new schema, implementing it in the codebase, and testing it to ensure it works as expected. I also worked on the migration of the data from the old schema to the new one, and on the integration of the new schema with the rest of the platform. The main challenge was doing this without creating any downtime in production.

impact.impact_1: Consolidates all events (primary and secondary), artists, venues, and inventory tracking into a single table
impact.impact_2: Opens the door to new features such as global events, and global inventory tracking
impact.impact_3: Improves the performance of the platform by 30%

title: Way of Santiago - Operations Research
description:
As part of my Industrial & Systems Engineering degree, I developed a project that uses Operations Research to find the most optimal stops to take when traveling the way of Santiago. If you are not aware of what the Way of Santiago is, here is a summary of it

The project was developed in Google Colab. The main challenge was collecting enough data, and developing the model by hand. After these, I was able to use pulp, a python linear programming library, to solve the problem.

Feel free to try it out yourself and see the code here.

impact.impact_1: Optimizes route planning across 6 different paths with ~100 stopping points using linear programming
impact.impact_2: Minimizes daily walking distance deviation based on user preferences (10-30km, 4-9 days)
impact.impact_3: Generates interactive downloadable maps and route summaries for optimal pilgrimage planning
